name: State capitalism
summary: State capitalism, in the programmatic sense, is an economy in which the state operates or controls businesses and steers investment while keeping markets, profit and often private firms as tools. Its adherents treat state ownership of strategic sectors and national champions as a route to development and national strength, and treat planning and markets as instruments rather than creeds. Politically it usually pairs with strong, insulated state authority, often under a single or dominant party.
scope: State capitalism as the defining sources use the term: an economy in which the state takes an active part in production and steers it for political ends (Britannica; The Economist's special report on its supporters), and Lenin's 1918-1921 programmatic use of it for a proletarian state controlling large industry while allowing supervised trade (The Tax in Kind; The Immediate Tasks). The Marxist and anarchist critique of the USSR, Nordic minority shareholdings, and what China, Singapore or the East Asian states did are other subjects or critics, not answers here.
